sponges text index | photo index Phylum Porifera Potato sponge
Biemna sp.*Family Desmacellidaeupdated Jul 2020

Where seen? Like a potato with eyes, this buried sponge is found on some of our shores near reefs. Features: Spherical, oval or irregular lumpy, 10-30cm, usually buried with only chimneys sticking out of the surface. Chimneys about 1cm in diameter, 1-2cm tall. The surface is uneven and very hairy which traps sediments and sand, camouflaging the sponge. Colour pale brown.


Terumbu Pempang Tengah, Jul 10


Terumbu Hantu, Apr 12


Beting Bronok, Jun 12

*Species are difficult to positively identify without close examination.
On this website, they are grouped by external features for convenience of display.
